english: A rough bloom of iron beaten out of a clay furnace. Full of slag and bad temper. It is not good metal. It is metal you made on day two.
Ground limestone and bone. Pulls the filth out of a melt and takes it to the surface. The blast furnace will not run without it.
Steel taken through a second heat and quenched properly. Holds an edge past the point where ordinary steel folds. Ironmonger work.
The end of the metal chain. Cuts stone like wet clay and shrugs off heat that would slump anything else. Weeks of furnace time in every ingot.
Machined to a tolerance nothing in this world can casually replace. Every powered thing worth owning wants a handful of these.
Cracked out of oil at a reagent bench. Light and stubborn and it does not rot - which puts it well ahead of most things left alive.
Hardened steel laminated into polymer backing. Stops what plate steel does not and weighs half as much doing it.
The neutral stock every medicine in the world now starts from. Unremarkable on its own. Nothing works without it.
Water-stained pages from somebody who understood furnaces. Half of it is missing. Gather enough and a drafting table can reconstruct what they knew.
A dispensary log kept long past the point it was any use to the person keeping it. The last entries are worth reading twice.
Load data and failure notes in three different hands. Whoever finished this document did not write the first half of it.
Pour schedules and load calculations. Somebody was building something to last. The pages stop before you find out whether it did.
A running inventory of what is worth stripping and what will kill you while you strip it. Practical to the last legible line.
Tracking notes and preservation methods from somebody who stayed out of towns on purpose. They lasted a long time.
Signed off by somebody who watched you make metal out of dirt. The forge is yours now. Consume it to take the Mark.
Signed off by somebody who never once heard you coming. The wilderness is yours now. Consume it to take the Mark.
Signed off by somebody who checked your stock and found it clean. People will owe you their lives. Consume it to take the Mark.
Signed off by somebody who watched you carry it all yourself. The ground is yours now. Consume it to take the Mark.
Signed off by somebody who counted. You did not freeze and you did not run dry. Consume it to take the Mark.
Signed off by somebody who could tell the difference between pulled and purchased. Consume it to take the Mark.
Clears an early infection if you catch it early. Past the second stage you are carrying a bottle of expensive brown water.
Real medicine made by somebody who knew what they were doing. Reverses a third stage infection. Ask the Apothecary nicely.
The only thing that brings a body back from a fourth stage infection. One person on this server can make it. Be good to them.
Clay and stone and patience. Smelts raw ore into crude iron. It is the worst furnace you will ever build and you will build it on day two.
Burns hot enough to make steel behave. Eats flux and coal in quantities that will define your week.
Turns stock metal into parts made to a tolerance. Everything with a motor in it starts here.
Glassware and a steady hand. The whole medical chain runs off this bench and so does everyone standing near it.
Reconstructs a working recipe out of enough damaged Field Notes. You cannot buy what comes off this table and you cannot perk your way to it.
You are standing in what came out of it. Health and stamina draining. Move.
Something nearby is making them stronger. Find it. It is not fighting back.
A cough and a tightness you can work through. Treat it now and it costs you a tincture. Leave it and it costs you more.
It is in you properly now. Stamina is going and it is not coming back on its own. A tincture will still hold it. Barely.
You are a liability to whoever you are standing next to. Nothing short of a real antibiotic turns this around.
You are dying and you can feel the schedule. One thing in the world reverses this and an Apothecary has to make it.
Smelt faster and pull more metal out of the same ore. The foundation every other Ironmonger perk sits on.
Hardened steel at rank 2. Carbide at rank 4. Nobody else on the server can make either of them.
Everything you forge comes off the anvil at a higher quality than it had any right to.
More rounds per batch and bulk casing recipes. The perk that keeps the Marshal in the fight.
Capstone. Blast furnace efficiency and the carbide recipes nobody else will ever see.
Dig faster and for longer. The ground stops being an obstacle and starts being a material.
Reinforced concrete tiers and faster cheaper building. What the base is actually made of.
More explosive damage and shaped charges. Also the only reliable answer to a Rotweaver.
Spikes and barricades and killbox blocks that actually have health worth counting.
Capstone. Repair structures mid-fight and unlock the fortification tier nobody else can build.
Make less noise and less light. Everything in the wilderness notices you later.
More meat and hide off every animal and the preservation recipes to stop it spoiling.
Trap blocks that hit harder and reset faster. The wilderness starts working for you.
Bow damage and draw speed and the advanced arrow tiers. Kills without telling the street.
Capstone. Crouched you are very nearly not there at all.
Firearm damage and handling and reload speed. The direct answer to most problems.
Composite armour tiers and better protection out of everything you wear.
Heavy weapon tiers and belt-fed conversions. Expensive to feed. Worth it.
Turret tiers and turrets that actually hit what they are aiming at.
Capstone. Everyone fighting near you fights better and you unlock what nobody else carries.
More output from every batch and the second reagent bench tier.
Tinctures at rank 1 and real antibiotics at rank 4. This is the perk that keeps people alive.
Everything medical heals more and applies faster including on other people.
Stimulants and gas ordnance and toxin coatings. Chemistry pointed outward for once.
Capstone. The serum. The only cure for a terminal infection anywhere in this world.
Strip vehicles and machinery faster and get considerably more out of them.
Better loot from every container you open. Quietly the strongest economy perk in the mod.
Electronics tiers and faster crafting of anything with wiring in it.
Vehicle tiers and fuel that lasts. Mobility is a survival stat from Cycle 3 onward.
Capstone. Field Notes turn up far more often and the salvage-only recipes open up.
A carbide head on a hardened steel haft. Goes through stone at a rate that makes the steel one feel like a joke. Only an Ironmonger will ever make you one.
Holds an edge through a working week. Expensive enough that you will notice when somebody borrows it.
Slow and enormous and it does not care what the thing in front of it is wearing. The melee answer to a Rotweaver if you are out of explosives.
Hardened steel laminated into polymer. Stops what plate steel does not and does not break your neck doing it.
The centrepiece of the Marshal's kit. Heavy enough to matter and light enough to run in.
Plated where it counts and articulated where it has to be. You will still feel every drop.
Belt-fed and appalling to feed. Enormous sustained output for as long as somebody keeps making you ammunition. Find an Ironmonger. Be nice to them.
Slow and precise and it does not care about armour. This is what a Rotweaver looks like from four hundred metres away.
Capstone. There is one of these per Marshal and everybody on the server knows who is carrying it.
Directional. Opens somebody else's wall without opening your own floor. Sapper work.
Moves an enormous amount of ground and barely bruises anything alive. It is a tool with a fuse. Do not bring it to a fight.
Salted and dried and it will still be food next week. The difference between a Trapper and a hungry group.
Dense and keeps forever and tastes like a punishment. What you carry when you are not coming back tonight.
A narrow hardened head made for punching plate. The Trapper's answer to Cycle 4 without touching a firearm.
A steel arrow dipped in something an Apothecary made. Neither of you can produce this alone. That is the point.
Two minutes of being considerably better at this followed by two minutes of being worse than you started. Choose the two minutes carefully.
Slows everything down including you. Handling and reloads improve sharply. Running does not.
Area denial in a tin. It leaves behind exactly what a Bloater leaves behind - which should tell you where the Apothecary got the idea.
Concentrated and unpleasant and it goes on anything with a point. The Apothecary's contribution to other people's weapons.
Pulled out of something dead and coaxed back into working. Everything with a thought in it needs one.
Optics and a circuit board and a great deal of patience. Goes into anything that has to notice something before you do.
Everything awkward about building a vehicle - boxed. The Scavenger makes these and the rest of the group stops walking.
Fuel that does not evaporate out of a rusted tank over a week. Goes considerably further than what you poured in.
Capstone. Strips a wreck in a fraction of the time and gets more out of it. Boring on paper and the most-used thing in the mod.
Concrete with iron running through it. Roughly twice the wall for not quite twice the work.
Poured properly with flux in the mix. This is what a Sapper builds when they intend to still be here in eight days.
They last. Wooden ones do not.
Stops movement without stopping line of sight. The Sapper's job is deciding where the horde walks and this is how you say it.
Capstone fortification. The only thing in this world that slows a Grinder down. It does not stop one.
A fixed gun that holds a corridor while you hold something else. The Marshal does not automate a position. They emplace it.
Loud and hungry for power and extremely effective in a doorway you chose on purpose.
Cheap and quiet and it resets. The wilderness starts working for you instead of at you.
Weight and timing and nothing else. Kills large things without telling the street about it.
The Apothecary's second tier. Everything the reagent bench cannot hold and everything the group cannot do without.
Damage and stamina and speed all up. There is a bill at the end of this and it is due in two minutes.
Handling and reloads sharply improved. Everything about moving is worse.
The bill. Stamina draining and everything harder than it was. Do not take another one.
Anyone can loot a forge. Build a bloomery and make metal out of dirt, then we will talk. Twenty blooms. I will know if you bought them.
You want the Ironmonger's mark. Everybody does. Go and make me twenty crude iron blooms out of ore you dug yourself.
Anyone can melt iron. Knowing what to put in with it is the trade. Limestone and bone, ground fine. Twelve.
Good. Now the part nobody bothers to learn. Twelve flux.
Last part. Twenty-five blooms delivered, and I do not care how tired you are. A smith who cannot make a delivery is a hobbyist. The forge is yours. Nobody else on this server makes hardened steel.
One more. Twenty-five blooms, delivered. On time.
Six animals. I am not going to tell you how - but if the whole street heard you do it, you are not a Trapper, you are a noise.
Everyone can shoot a deer. Take six animals and do it quietly.
Forty meat, and it had better not be crawling by the time it gets here. Knowing how to carry it is half the job.
Now bring it back. Forty meat. Unspoiled.
Twelve more. One good week is luck. Two is a Trapper. The wilderness is yours. Go and be quiet in it.
Last part. Twelve more. Then the wilderness is yours.
Build the bench. Make the base. Eight of them, clean, no shortcuts - if the stock is dirty then everything you make from it is a lie.
Medicine starts a long way before medicine. Eight reagent base.
Six polymer. It is not medicine and that is the point - a chemist who can only make one thing is not a chemist.
Now something that is not a cure. Six polymer stock.

Twelve delivered. There will come a night when somebody's life is the difference between you having stock and not. Get used to holding it. The bench is yours. People are going to owe you their lives. Be decent about it.
Twelve reagent base, delivered. Then people start depending on you.
A hundred cement. It is boring and it is heavy and that is the entire discipline. If this puts you off, good - better now than later.
Nothing about this trade is exciting. A hundred cement.
Produce one hundred and fifty more
Another hundred and fifty. Yes, really. Whatever you are planning to build, it needs more than you think and it needs it before dark.
Again. A hundred and fifty. You are learning what a wall costs.
Deliver one hundred and twenty cement
Carry it here. All of it. A Sapper who cannot move material is somebody who draws nice plans. The ground is yours. Decide where they walk.
Bring me a hundred and twenty. Carried, not traded.
Sixty. Not clever, not subtle. I need to know you do not freeze, and there is only one way to find that out.
Sixty of them. That is the whole instruction.
Put down one hundred and twenty more
Another hundred and twenty. Anybody can win one fight. I am looking for somebody who is still standing on the twentieth.
Again, and double. Winning once proves nothing.
Deliver one hundred and fifty gunpowder

Now the part that actually kills people: supply. A hundred and fifty powder. Every Marshal who died out there died with an empty gun. The line is yours. Hold it, and keep somebody making your ammunition.
Last part, and the one that matters. A hundred and fifty powder.
Forty mechanical parts, out of things other people gave up on. Do not buy them. I will be able to tell.
Forty mechanical parts. Pulled, not purchased.
Thirty electrical. Harder, and in worse places. That is where the trade actually lives.
Now thirty electrical. They are not lying in the road.

Sixty paper. Laugh if you want. Everything anybody knew is written down somewhere, and the person who brings it back decides who learns it. The ruins are yours. Everything out there is worth more in your hands.
Sixty paper. You will understand why later.
Plant it, water it, wait. Fibre and oil in one plant. The Trapper gets cloth out of it and the chemist gets something to crack, which is why it is the first thing worth putting in the ground.
Fibre and oil in one plant. The Trapper gets cloth out of it and the chemist gets something to crack, which is why it is the first thing worth putting in the ground.
Flax, growing. Leave it alone until it is ready.
Plant it, water it, wait. Hardy, ugly, and it grows where nothing else will. Flour for the road and mash for the still.
Hardy, ugly, and it grows where nothing else will. Flour for the road and mash for the still.
Rye, growing. Leave it alone until it is ready.
Plant it, water it, wait. The medicinal one. Bitter enough that nobody eats it by accident and useful enough that the Apothecary will ask where you got it.
The medicinal one. Bitter enough that nobody eats it by accident and useful enough that the Apothecary will ask where you got it.
Comfrey, growing. Leave it alone until it is ready.
Plant it, water it, wait. Grown for the press, not the plate. What comes out of it runs an engine or becomes plastic.
Grown for the press, not the plate. What comes out of it runs an engine or becomes plastic.
Rapeseed, growing. Leave it alone until it is ready.
Pressed out of flax or rapeseed. Feeds the polymer chain and burns clean enough to run a motor, which makes a field into a fuel supply.
Coarse and grey and it keeps. The first half of every meal you will eat away from home.
Rye mash run through a still. Undrinkable on purpose - it is a solvent, and it is the reason the Apothecary no longer has to find acid to work.
Rot and plant matter turned into something that grows things. The Husk finally contributes.
Flour and water and nothing else. It will not spoil, it will not excite you, and it will still be edible when everything in your pack is not.
Boiled out of what the butchering left behind. Thin, but it is hot and it is not rotten, and on day two that is the whole review.
Comfrey and bone. Takes the edge off an infection for a while - the shakes stop and you can work. It does not cure anything. Only the Apothecary does that, and you should still go and see them.
Everything the drying rack made, boxed for somebody who is not coming back tonight.
Pale, chalky, and soft enough to work with a bad pickaxe. Burns down to the flux that makes a furnace behave. There is a reason old towns were built where this is.
Black, sticky, and it smells like a road in August. Cracks down into most of the useful plastics if you have the bench and the patience.

Bright yellow crust off the edge of a burnt seam. Everything about it says do not breathe this. It is also the difference between an Apothecary who is working and one who is waiting on a looted bottle of acid.
Heavy, dull, and worth the walk. Tungsten ore, and the only honest road to carbide. It is in the wasteland and nowhere else, which is not an accident.
A pale shelf of rock breaking the surface. Chalky, soft, and worth stopping for.
Tar pushing up through cracked ground, still slow-moving in the heat. The smell carries further than the stain does.
Yellow rime over a burnt seam. Stand upwind and take what you need.
A dull grey seam threading through the rock. Hard going, a long way from anywhere, and the top of the metal chain starts here.
Rot goes in and soil comes out. Slow and it smells, which is roughly the deal with everything that works.
Air and time and salt. The Trapper's station - preserving stops being a recipe you happen to know and becomes a thing you built.
A proper meal, for once. Stamina and recovery both up for a good while.
The shakes have stopped and you can work. You are still infected - this only bought you time.

Dawn, and the count is wrong. What came out of the treeline was dry as paper and twice as quick - no weight to it at all, just speed and appetite. The Husks are in the world now. Nothing that arrives leaves again.
It came apart in the doorway and the air was still wrong an hour later. Sat down on the stairs and could not stop coughing. Fighting them in your own hallway is no longer free. Bloaters.
Tracks in the ash this morning. Four sets, spread wide, moving parallel. They have stopped coming at me and started coming around me. Open ground is no longer a way home. Carrion Hounds.

Put most of a magazine into it and it kept walking. Whatever is under that skin was not there last week. Shooting my way out is over as a plan - the next answer has to be built, not bought. Rotweavers.

Nothing woke me. That is the part worth being afraid of. It was already inside and it made no sound doing it. Night is not time to work in any more; night is time to be somewhere with one door. The Hollow.
One of them hung back and never came forward, and everything around it hit harder for exactly as long as it lived. The horde has a shape now. Kill the thing at the back first. Choirs.

It came through the wall. Not over it. Not around it. Through. There is no box left to build that ends this, so stop building boxes - learn the ground, keep the fuel topped up, and know the hour you leave. Grinders.
Iron-bound and heavy enough that nothing drags it off. Holds considerably more than the crate you nailed together on day one.
Steel shelving on a machined frame. The warehouse the workshop paid for - and by the time you can build one you will need it.
